Rs. 451 billion, zero loans: Cabinet approves two new expressways

cards.what_happened: The Cabinet approved two new expressway projects worth Rs. 451 billion, to be built without loans using tax revenue. The projects are the Kurunegala–Galewela Expressway, the first section of Phase 4 of the Central Expressway, and the Kahathuduwa–Ingiriya Expressway, the first phase of the proposed Ruwanpura Expressway. Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake announced the approval in a social media post.
details: According to Newswire, Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake said the government is undertaking major expressway development projects worth Rs. 451 billion. He made the announcement in a social media post.
The projects will be financed without any loans, using tax revenue to cover the costs. The minister described the investment as significant for road infrastructure, fully funded through tax revenue.

The Cabinet approved the Kurunegala–Galewela Expressway, which is the first section of Phase 4 of the Central Expressway. It also approved the Kahathuduwa–Ingiriya Expressway, the first phase of the proposed Ruwanpura Expressway.
key_facts: Government approves two expressway projects worth Rs. 451 billion.
Projects will be funded by tax revenue, no loans.
Kurunegala–Galewela Expressway is first section of Phase 4 of Central Expressway.
Kahathuduwa–Ingiriya Expressway is first phase of proposed Ruwanpura Expressway.
Announcement made by Minister Bimal Rathnayake on social media.
cards.blurb: Cabinet approves two expressway projects worth Rs. 451 billion, funded by tax revenue without loans.
cards.spoken: Good morning, listeners. The government has approved two new expressway projects worth Rs. 451 billion. Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayake announced the approval on social media, saying the projects will be built without loans, using tax revenue. The first project is the Kurunegala–Galewela Expressway, the first section of Phase 4 of the Central Expressway. The second is the Kahathuduwa–Ingiriya Expressway, the first phase of the proposed Ruwanpura Expressway. The Cabinet gave its approval, and the minister described the investment as significant for road infrastructure. The report is from Newswire.

Sudanese army air attack kills 13 in western Sudan: Rights group

cards.what_happened: The Sudanese Armed Forces launched an air strike that killed at least 13 civilians in the Abu Qalb area of West Kordofan. The victims included women and children, and several homes were destroyed.
details: The Sudanese Armed Forces, or SAF, launched an air strike. The strike killed at least 13 civilians in the Abu Qalb area of West Kordofan state, and the victims included women and children, according to the Emergency Lawyers rights group.

The warplanes from the military government attacked the Abu Zabad locality. The strike happened the day before Monday, and Emergency Lawyers said several homes were destroyed in the strike, which they described in a social media post on Monday after preliminary monitoring, but Al Jazeera was unable to immediately verify the report.

Emergency Lawyers said the continued use of indiscriminate airstrikes on residential areas poses a direct threat to civilian lives and is a grave violation of international humanitarian law. The group documents human rights violations and cited videos of horrific scenes of destruction. Mohamed Didan, the official spokesperson for the Special Operations Forces that fight alongside the SAF, said on Facebook that his troops moved through Abu Zabad and eliminated RSF positions in West Kordofan.

The war between the army and the RSF began in April 2023 and has created one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, according to several aid organisations. Reports say the war has killed at least 59,000 people, displaced about 13 million and pushed parts of the country into famine, while much fighting is concentrated in Darfur and Kordofan and recently shifted towards the Blue Nile province. Drone warfare has surged during the war and become the deadliest threat to civilians, experts said both sides are being supplied with drones by countries in the Middle East and beyond, and the SAF has gained control over several strategically important villages and localities in West Kordofan recently.
key_facts: Sudanese army warplanes killed at least 13 civilians in West Kordofan.
Victims included women and children, several homes destroyed.
Emergency Lawyers said airstrike was grave legal violation.
Mohamed Didan said troops eliminated RSF positions.
War began April 2023 and killed at least 59,000 people.
War displaced about 13 million and pushed parts into famine.
Drone warfare surged and became deadliest threat to civilians.
SAF gained control of several West Kordofan villages recently.
cards.blurb: Sudanese army air attack in West Kordofan killed 13 civilians including women and children.
cards.spoken: Here is the scene. A war is still going on in Sudan. The army there used warplanes in an air strike. The strike hit the Abu Zabad area in West Kordofan. It killed at least thirteen civilians. The victims included women and children. A local rights group called Emergency Lawyers said several homes were destroyed. They said the continued use of airstrikes on homes is a threat to civilian lives and breaks international law. The army's special operations forces also said they moved through the area and removed what they called RSF positions. The wider war began in April twenty twenty three. It has caused a big humanitarian crisis. Reports say it has killed at least fifty-nine thousand people and displaced about thirteen million.
